question: Should OpenClaw add first-class outbound recipient allowlist policy for Slack/core sends, or keep this as an optional plugin using message_sending hooks?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public outbound authorization config under a documented trusted-operator security model.

options.title: Add first-class outbound target policy
options.body: Add an allowTo-style policy with schema, docs, tests, and send-boundary enforcement while keeping allowFrom inbound-only.

options.title: Route to plugin
options.body: Publish or point to a ClawHub plugin that cancels non-allowlisted sends through message_sending hooks.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track this as a Slack-specific acceptance case under #87870 so recipient authorization, sanitization, and verified delivery are designed together.

recommendation.title: Add first-class outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add an allowTo-style policy with schema, docs, tests, and send-boundary enforcement while keeping allowFrom inbound-only.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior trusted-operator security triage and outbound policy history make steipete the best available owner for the product/security boundary choice.
